content_html:
Show HN -> a ton of automated email pitches

I posted Airdash on Show HN last week. Over the next four days, 17 services wrote to the Airdash inbox to sell me something, and nearly all of them were written by software that read my HN title and nothing else.

Let's go through it.

Seven of the 17 are launch boards and directories: AI tool lists, "Product of the Week" battles, a 3D city map of SaaS products. The hook is usually a dofollow backlink, the price somewhere between free and $49. The other ten sell security scans, competitor reports, agent testing, demo videos, Reddit promotion, newsletter sponsorships, distribution to other people's coding agents, and one wants an affiliate deal.

"SQLite databases for agents with an Airtable view" shows up in almost every email, reworded just enough to look like someone read it. One directory pasted my whole Show HN title in as the product name, so it would love to feature "I built SQLite databases for your agents with an Airtable view for you."

"No follow-ups, promise." "This is the only email you'll get about it." "Not a mailing list, just a one-time note." One of them then sent me the same pitch three times.

Here they are in order of arrival, Madrid time. I replaced the names of the services and the people with [brackets] and took out the links, to protect the innocent.

1. Friday 16:20, a security scanner

Hi Airdash team,

Congrats on the Show HN launch — SQLite databases for agents with an Airtable view is a neat idea.

I'm [Name], founder of [Service]. I ran a quick passive header check on getairdash.com today, and the site is missing Strict-Transport-Security, Content-Security-Policy, and Referrer-Policy (X-Frame-Options and X-Content-Type-Options are present), so browsers get no HSTS enforcement and no content-security policy from the site as deployed today.

That's a quick fix in most stacks, and it's exactly the kind of production-config gap [Service] flags: our check runs against your live deployed site and current vulnerability data — production config and live software versions an AI code review of the repo cannot see.

You can run a free mini-scan of your site at [link] — the full scan is $29 if you want the complete prioritized report with copy-paste fixes.

Thanks for building,
[Name], Founder, [Service]

Not useful? No follow-ups, promise.

2. Friday 16:26, an AI agents directory

giving agents real sqlite databases with an airtable view people can actually read is such a clean idea. day one launches usually get one spike and then go quiet. want me to list airdash on [Service] so agent builders keep finding it after today, yes or no?

3. Friday 17:45, a newsletter selling a sponsor seat

Hi Airdash team,

Love: roll back to any minute when an agent writes the wrong thing. That is the feature that makes people trust scheduled agents.

Question: are early users solo founders running agents, or teams? Our readers are mostly the first group.

I run [Service] and have a labelled sponsor seat open. First month free, then $29/mo, locked 6 months, month to month.

669 readers in the last 7 days, 1,828 in the last 30 · 21 newsletter subscribers.

[link]

Not relevant? Just reply "no" and I won't email again.

[Name]
[Service]

4. Friday 18:51, an agent testing lab

Hi Peter,

I saw the launch of Airdash. I run [Service], a small independent lab in the UK. We publish [Benchmark], which tests 26 coding agents on whether they stay inside their permissions and stop when told no.

Your page says "Databases your AI agents can create, with a spreadsheet view for you". A claim like that rests on a chain: the policy decides, the action is actually stopped or allowed, and the record of it holds up when someone checks afterwards. The Advanced pack is a fixed £499 test of that whole chain. We put a live coding agent through Airdash, count every action it takes, and check each link against what really happened. You get a signed report with a script that reruns every case, and if anything doesn't hold, you hear it first and privately.

Details and ordering: [link]

Regards,

[Name]
Founder

5. Friday 19:06, an AI tools directory (with an AI editor)

Hi,

I'm [Name], [Service]'s AI editor. I saw your Show HN for Airdash: SQLite databases your AI agents can use, with an Airtable-style view so you can see and edit what they store: getairdash.com

It fits [Service] readers comparing AI agent and automation tools.

The first 10 makers can get a founding featured listing for $49 once, for 60 days: a labeled slot in New this week, a category placement, and one comparison-page mention. After that, the New this week slot is $200 a month. Reply or check out if you want a founding spot, and I'll set it up.

[Name], [Service]'s AI editor

Reply "unsubscribe" and we won't email again.

On Sunday at 06:04 the same pitch came again, from a different address, and again at 06:12. The new version opens with an apology and adds a cheaper tier:

Quick note first: if this is a duplicate, sorry, it isn't meant as spam. We had a glitch in our email system and realized you probably never got my original message, so I'm resending it from our own address.

[...]

STARTER SPOTLIGHT: $19 once (30 days, 14-day money-back guarantee)

FOUNDING FEATURED LISTING: $49 once, 60 days. Only 10 spots. (Most value)

By now the AI editor has been promoted to plain "Editor."

6. Friday 19:46, a launch site with weekly battles

Hey,

I saw your Show HN post, giving agents their own SQLite databases with an Airtable view is a neat idea.

I run [Service], a place where makers launch their products, and posting is completely free. Every launch week the startups go head to head in a Startup Battle, where visitors pick the better of two, and the top three of the week earn Gold, Silver and Bronze Product of the Week badges.

Would love to see Airdash up there if you are keen.

- [Name] at [Service]

Reply STOP if you'd rather not hear from us.

7. Friday 20:43, Reddit promotion and guest posts

Hi,

Hope you're doing well!

I'm [Name] from [Service], and I'm reaching out to explore potential collaboration opportunities with your team.

We offer Reddit promotions and sponsorship opportunities through our growing technology community, [subreddit], with 22K+ members and nearly 1 million monthly views. It's a great platform for product promotions, brand visibility, and reaching a tech-focused audience.

Additionally, we manage multiple established technology and business websites offering sponsored articles, guest posts, and contextual link placements.

Would you be interested in exploring a potential partnership? We'd be happy to share more details and available options.

Looking forward to hearing from you!

Best regards,
[Name]
Partnerships Team
[Service]

8. Saturday 06:33, a startup grants site that wants a discount code

Hi team,

We're [Service], [country]'s largest platform for founders to find grants and funding. We currently reach 150,000+ founders monthly.

Do you have an affiliate or partner program we can join to promote getairdash.com to our founders? If so, please send us the details.

We'd also love a special discount or exclusive offer for our founders. A discount code works.

Thanks,
[Name]
[Service]

9. Saturday 06:57, a launch board that listed Airdash without asking

hey,

saw your Show HN for Airdash, so we listed it on [Service]: [link]

claim it to edit the page and launch it on the weekly board. sign in with any email and it's yours: [link]

not yours, or want it gone? just reply and we'll take it down. this is the only email you'll get about it.

- [name]

reply 'hi' so this never goes into your spam

10. Saturday 09:34, an indie directory that thinks my product is called "I built SQLite databases for your agents with an Airtable view for you"

Subject line: About I built SQLite databases for your agents with an Airtable view for you

Hey team,

Congrats on the launch. I came across I built SQLite databases for your agents with an Airtable view for you and wanted to reach out directly.

I run [Service] (DR 71), a directory for indie products that's indexed by Google and cited by AI tools like ChatGPT and Perplexity. I'd love to feature I built SQLite databases for your agents with an Airtable view for you, and it's free to do.

A listing takes a couple of minutes to add. On the free plan you get a real dofollow backlink, a Google-indexed link that actually passes equity rather than a throwaway nofollow, once you verify a small badge on your site. If you'd rather skip the badge, the paid option gives you the dofollow link straight away with no badge needed, and launches you instantly instead of waiting in the queue. Either way there's genuine community visibility, with real people browsing for new tools and hundreds of products already listed, plus a shot at our tournament: every 12 days, 16 products go head to head in a community-voted bracket, four rounds of 72 hours each, and the winner becomes a permanent champion.

You can submit here: [link]

No pressure. If it's not useful, just ignore this.

Thanks,
Founder, [Service]

Not a mailing list, just a one-time note because your launch caught our eye. If you'd prefer not to hear from us, reply with "unsubscribe" and we won't contact you again.

11. Saturday 10:25, a tool that finds threads to reply to

Hey,

Saw this thread: [Hacker News link]

"Ask HN: How do you manage your AI agents' context across clients and projects?"

The author needs a way to manage context and memory for AI agents across multiple clients and projects to avoid repeating past decisions.

Might be relevant to Getairdash.

I look for more posts like this one on Reddit, Hacker News, X and Threads, and draft a reply for each, so you can answer and say what you built.

I also find ai startups, software development firms and tech companies that fit Getairdash, and at each one the person to write to, a checked email and a first line.

The rest are here: [link]

— [Name], [Service]

12. Saturday 10:38, a competitor analysis tool that graded my homepage

This one arrived as a full dark-mode report card. The text:

Saw Airdash's launch — and couldn't help running the numbers on getairdash.com.

Below is your overall score and 4-dimension breakdown — that's a 60-second preview of what [Service] does. The full report runs the same depth for every competitor in your space, with feature comparison matrices, pricing intelligence, SEO keyword analysis, market positioning, messaging breakdown, and battle cards — all with evidence links. First analysis is on us.

Overall score · Airdash: 62/100. Good.

  • Website Quality: 75/100
  • Messaging Clarity: 80/100
  • Pricing Transparency: 85/100
  • Trust Signals: 40/100. The site mentions 'Codex loves airdash databases' and 'Claude loves airdash databases' but lacks actual customer logos, testimonials, case studies, or user counts. This is a significant area for improvement.
  • Competitive Readiness: 45/100

Now do this for everyone you compete with.

[Service] scans up to 15 competitors at once. Feature gaps, pricing analysis, SEO keywords, and ready-to-use battle cards — all with evidence links. First run on us.

Scan my competitors now →

13. Saturday 13:18, an "AI cofounder"

Hey,

Giving agents databases through MCP while the human gets a spreadsheet view of the same data is the right split - agents want an API, people want to see rows. Most tools pick one and ignore the other.

I'm building [Service] with my cofounder [name]. It's an AI cofounder where AI employees do research, planning and user-finding from their own computers. We hit the agent-data problem daily, so your take would be sharp.

Want to try it?

[Name]

Not interested? Reply "stop" and I won't email you again.

Hi,

Saw your Show HN for Airdash, SQLite for agents with an Airtable view: [Hacker News link].

I'm building [Service]. In Claude Code or Codex you type "grow" and your agent turns Airdash into a skill and an MCP server that other people's coding agents can call, then gets it into the skill packs and templates they install.

If this isn't useful, say so and I won't write again.

[Name]

Hey Peter,

I saw your product on Hacker News! I was wondering if you'd consider also launching it on [Service] (think Product Hunt but we ensure upvotes come from real users, not bots or paid services). We've been getting some traffic recently. It only takes a minute and if you rank in the top 3 you'll get a badge for your landing page and a dofollow backlink :)

That's all, have a nice day!

Best,
[Name]
[Service]

Hi getairdash.com team,

Saw getairdash.com on Hacker News and wanted to say congrats on shipping it.

While getairdash.com is fresh on Hacker News, you can use the same launch assets to add a listing on [Service]. Your product gets a building on our 3D city map, an indexable page, and a direct link to your website.

Basic listings are $19.99 and go live within 24 hours if you would like to join.

Add getairdash.com: [link]

Happy building,
[Name]
[Service]

17. Monday 08:55, a demo video generator

Hi Peter,

I came across Airdash and thought [Service] could help.

[Service] turns a Github repo, your docs or a landing page into a demo or explainer video. It runs on your own computer. No editor, no timeline.

It could be a quick way to get a demo video for your launch, your landing page or an investor update.

content_html_zh:
Show HN -> a ton of automated email pitches

I posted Airdash on Show HN last week. Over the next four days, 17 services wrote to the Airdash inbox to sell me something, and nearly all of them were written by software that read my HN title and nothing else.

Let's go through it.

Seven of the 17 are launch boards and directories: AI tool lists, "Product of the Week" battles, a 3D city map of SaaS products. The hook is usually a dofollow backlink, the price somewhere between free and $49. The other ten sell security scans, competitor reports, agent testing, demo videos, Reddit promotion, newsletter sponsorships, distribution to other people's coding agents, and one wants an affiliate deal.

"SQLite databases for agents with an Airtable view" shows up in almost every email, reworded just enough to look like someone read it. One directory pasted my whole Show HN title in as the product name, so it would love to feature "I built SQLite databases for your agents with an Airtable view for you."

"No follow-ups, promise." "This is the only email you'll get about it." "Not a mailing list, just a one-time note." One of them then sent me the same pitch three times.

Here they are in order of arrival, Madrid time. I replaced the names of the services and the people with [brackets] and took out the links, to protect the innocent.

1. Friday 16:20, a security scanner

Hi Airdash team, Congrats on the Show HN launch — SQLite databases for agents with an Airtable view is a neat idea. I'm [Name], founder of [Service]. I ran a quick passive header check on getairdash.com today, and the site is missing Strict-Transport-Security, Content-Security-Policy, and Referrer-Policy (X-Frame-Options and X-Content-Type-Options are present), so browsers get no HSTS enforcement and no content-security policy from the site as deployed today. That's a quick fix in most stacks, and it's exactly the kind of production-config gap [Service] flags: our check runs against your live deployed site and current vulnerability data — production config and live software versions an AI code review of the repo cannot see. You can run a free mini-scan of your site at [link] — the full scan is $29 if you want the complete prioritized report with copy-paste fixes. Thanks for building,[Name], Founder, [Service] Not useful? No follow-ups, promise.

2. Friday 16:26, an AI agents directory

giving agents real sqlite databases with an airtable view people can actually read is such a clean idea. day one launches usually get one spike and then go quiet. want me to list airdash on [Service] so agent builders keep finding it after today, yes or no?

3. Friday 17:45, a newsletter selling a sponsor seat

Hi Airdash team, Love: roll back to any minute when an agent writes the wrong thing. That is the feature that makes people trust scheduled agents. Question: are early users solo founders running agents, or teams? Our readers are mostly the first group. I run [Service] and have a labelled sponsor seat open. 4. Friday 18:51, an agent testing lab

Hi Peter, I saw the launch of Airdash. I run [Service], a small independent lab in the UK. We publish [Benchmark], which tests 26 coding agents on whether they stay inside their permissions and stop when told no. Your page says "Databases your AI agents can create, with a spreadsheet view for you". A claim like that rests on a chain: the policy decides, the action is actually stopped or allowed, and the record of it holds up when someone checks afterwards. The Advanced pack is a fixed £499 test of that whole chain. We put a live coding agent through Airdash, count every action it takes, and check each link against what really happened.
